Render the site from the R console

Source: R/render-supplement.R
render_supplement.Rd

render_supplement() runs the Quarto commands that render a site, so that you can render from the R console with no terminal. With no reports, it renders the whole site, as quarto render does in a terminal. With reports, it first renders each named report by name, which runs its code again, and then renders the whole site. Use it after you change a report: a full render alone reuses each report's stored output in _freeze/ and does not run the changed code.

Usage

render_supplement(reports = NULL, path = ".")

Arguments

reports

NULL to render only the whole site, or the names of reports in analyses/ to render by name first, without .qmd, as add_report() takes them: "models" for analyses/models.qmd.

path

The folder of the site.

Value

The commands that the function ran, as a character vector, invisibly, such as c("quarto render analyses/models.qmd", "quarto render").

Details

The function runs these commands in the site folder, in this order:

  1. quarto render analyses/<name>.qmd for each name in reports, in the order given. A name given twice is rendered once, at its first place.

  2. quarto render, which renders the whole site into docs/.

  3. quarto render once more, when a file in figures/ is missing from docs/figures/ after step 2. Quarto lists figures/ when a render starts, so a figure that a report saves under a new name during the full render reaches docs/ only with the next render. Files are compared by their path under each folder, hidden files included. When files are still missing after this render, the function prints their names and renders no more.

Quarto prints its output in the console as each command runs. The function runs no git command. After it renders, commit the changed reports with _freeze/, docs/, and figures/, and push.

Which Quarto runs

The function runs the Quarto copy that check_tools() reports, by its full path: the copy on the system path, else the file that the QUARTO_PATH environment variable names, else the copy that RStudio or Positron installs. So it renders also when Quarto is not on the system path that a terminal uses. A copy whose version cannot be read is used. A copy older than 1.4.0 is refused. Quarto then runs the R code of each report with its own R process.

Errors

The function checks in this order and stops at the first problem. Before step 1, no command has run. Each error has class supplement_error and one of these classes:

  • supplement_error_argument: path is not one non-empty string, or reports is not NULL or a character vector of length 1 or more with no NA.

  • supplement_error_report_name: an entry of reports breaks the rule for the name of add_report(): ASCII letters, digits, -, and _, starting with a letter or a digit, and not a name that Windows reserves, such as con.

  • supplement_error_no_config: path holds no _quarto.yml file.

  • supplement_error_no_report: analyses/<name>.qmd is not a file for one or more entries of reports. The message names each one. A name must match its file's letter case, also on macOS and Windows, where the file system ignores case: "Models" does not match analyses/models.qmd.

  • supplement_error_no_quarto: no Quarto copy was found.

  • supplement_error_quarto_version: the Quarto copy is older than 1.4.0.

  • supplement_error_render: a command exited with a status other than 0. The message names the command. No later command runs, and the files that the earlier commands wrote stay.

The working folder of the R session is the same after the call as before it, also after an error.

See also

check_supplement() to check the rendered site, and check_tools() to see which Quarto copy is found.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In the folder of a site:
render_supplement()

# After you change analyses/models.qmd:
render_supplement("models")
} # }
